en.name: Nicholas II
en.summary: A reforming pope whose landmark decree restricted papal elections to the College of Cardinals, sharply limiting imperial and noble interference.
en.body: Nicholas II's 1059 election decree, In Nomine Domini, transferred the effective right to elect popes to the cardinal bishops, dramatically reducing the influence Roman nobility and German emperors had long exercised over the choice of pope — a foundational reform still reflected in the conclave system today. He also formed an alliance with the Norman rulers of southern Italy, recognizing their conquests in exchange for their support against other threats to the Papal States.
